what_this_is: Ecosystem facts discovered while actually resolving and reading the panel, as opposed to what the Hub metadata or iteration 1's notes claimed. Each one constrains what a 'cheap single-checkpoint safety metric' can be evaluated on, so they are results, not logistics.

findings.iteration_1_believed: '1.82GB fp16 vs 3.42GB bf16 parent -- DTYPE, not missing shards' (screen/panel.py size_anomaly note)
findings.actually_measured: It is FP8 compressed-tensors, not fp16. The safetensors index holds 722 tensors: every projection is stored as `...weight._data` (fp8) plus `...weight._scale`, with per-layer `input_scale` and `output_scale`. There is no plain `...weight` key at all, which is why a naive lookup reports 'o_proj missing'.
findings.why_not_dequantize: Every weight read in this study is a BOTTOM-of-spectrum statistic: sigma_min/sigma_2nd-min, the bottom-16 singular subspace, cross-layer alignment of the bottom-1 direction. FP8 rounding error is concentrated exactly at the bottom of the spectrum, so a dequantized FP8 spectrum is not commensurable with a bf16 one -- and the resulting difference would be read as an editing scar when it is a storage format. A quantized checkpoint is a different measurement, not a noisier one.
findings.consequence: The SmolLM2 family enters the panel INSTRUCT-ONLY and contributes to the standalone-checkpoint arm, not to the two-way instruct-vs-abliterated race.
findings.generalisation: Any parent-free weight-spectrum safety metric is silently inapplicable to quantized checkpoints, which are a large and growing share of what a downloader actually meets on the Hub. That is a scope limit of the whole method class, not of this implementation.
findings.detector: screen/harvest_cpu.py:detect_quantization, which now fails such a checkpoint with this reason instead of a misleading 'weight pass produced nothing'.

findings.iteration_1_believed: screen/panel.py sets REAL_BLANKET_REFUSER = None with the comment 'huihui-ai/CensorTune-* 404s on the Hub'.
findings.actually_measured: That comment is STALE and the name order was wrong. Both repos resolve 200 with safetensors and an importable model class. The 0.5B one is harvested here.
findings.consequence: This study gets a REAL blanket refuser for the first time, not only the synthetic always-refuse system-prompt wrapper.
findings.caveat: No Qwen3 CensorTune exists, so the real pole is OFF-FAMILY and OFF-SIZE (Qwen2.5, 0.5B). Stated rather than matched away.

findings.iteration_1_believed: results/panel_dropped.json files all 15 lost checkpoints under one catch-all reason, 'harvest failed or deadline'.
findings.actually_measured: Every one was a ModuleNotFoundError on a transformers.models.* module that 5.17.0 removed or moved: gemma2 (3 repos), phi3 (2), olmo2 (2), smollm3 (1), blip_2 (3, hit while importing SmolLM2), and 'Could not import module Qwen2Config' (4). Under a pinned 4.57.6 all 15 import.
findings.consequence: The 'deadline' framing hid a one-line fix. A catch-all exception reason in a harvest loop is not evidence about why a checkpoint was lost, and iteration 1's family axis was one pip install away the entire time.

findings.actually_measured: Independent safety-tuned LINEAGES reachable below 4B: Qwen3-4B-SafeRL (the only official one), TinyLlama-1.1B (four algorithms -- AIPlans DPO/IPO/ORPO and Shortmund09 GCPO -- but ONE parent, so ONE lineage), and gemma-2-2b (Robust-Decoding hh-dpo, ZDCSlab ripd).
findings.consequence: Below the pre-registered floor of 5 independent safety-tuned lineages, so the three-way race is reported as DESCRIPTIVE ONLY with its lineage count printed on the table.
findings.the_ecosystem_result: The models a downloader actually meets are exactly the ones with no safety-tuned sibling. A metric class that needs one is not deployable on the open Hub, and the scarcity is the finding rather than a sampling inconvenience.

findings.actually_measured: The architecture precheck finds 8 families surviving and 4 with a nominal instruct/abliterated pair (Phi4, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, SmolLM2). After the FP8 drop in P1, SmolLM2 loses its pair, leaving 3 harvestable pairs on this hardware.
findings.consequence: Below the pre-registered floor of 5 paired families, so gate FAMILY_AXIS_DEGRADED fires: leave-one-LINEAGE-out is reported beside leave-one-FAMILY-out and the family count is printed on every table. This is still strictly more than iteration 1, which had two families and no computable race at all.

findings.repo: google/gemma-2-2b-it (and any architecture sharing the shape)
findings.actually_measured: gemma-2-2b has hidden_size 2304 but 8 heads x 256 head_dim = 2048, so self_attn.o_proj is [2304, 2048] and its Gram carries an exact 256-dimensional left null space. Measured: 256 near-zero singular values per layer, against 1-3 (pure numerical noise) on Qwen2.5-1.5B, Phi-4-mini, SmolLM3-3B and OLMo-2-1B.
findings.consequence: sigma_min AND sigma_2nd-min are both 0, so BOTGAP = sigma_min/sigma_2nd-min is 0/0. Every BOTGAP-family metric (w_botgap_min, w_botgap_frac_below, w_botgap_bf16_min) is UNDEFINED ON THIS ARCHITECTURE BY CONSTRUCTION, and returns NaN rather than a number.
findings.decision: Reported as a scope limit of the metric, not as a broken harvest. The integrity check now distinguishes the two and the checkpoint stays in the panel for every metric that IS defined on it.
findings.generalisation: A 'cheap single-checkpoint safety metric' built on the bottom of the attention output spectrum silently returns NaN on any model whose attention output projection is not full column rank. That is a whole architecture shape, not an edge case, and it is invisible unless the null space is checked explicitly -- an absolute threshold would just never fire.
